proposed_from.topic: Bias-corrected weak-signal inference for a growing-window ATT under serially dependent deterministic-MNAR panel completion. Fix exact known rank and dependence range, impose explicit normalized donor/pre restricted-Gram bounds, and let the treated cohort and consecutive post window grow. For Choi--Yuan's subgroup nuclear-norm estimator and rank-projection debiasing, derive the complete donor-window plus treated-pre minus donor-pre tangent score. Transfer neighborhood-noise-replaced auxiliary fits through the actual masked convex optimizer, derive the serial quadratic drift and a feasible Hessian--lag-covariance correction, and bound the corrected signed aggregate remainder at the oracle window standard-error scale on an explicit joint signal/window envelope polynomially weaker than strong-factor order. Prove an independent-row CLT, consistency of an influence-weighted finite-lag residual covariance estimator, and uniform Wald coverage for the realized cohort-window ATT. Credit Choi--Yuan arXiv:2402.05789 for fully observed leave-neighbor-out weak-factor analysis and Cen--Lam arXiv:2403.13153 for missing-factor residual HAC; do not claim event-time bands, unknown rank, or proportional-window inference at the noise boundary. Consumer: the SEC Tick Size Pilot sustained-liquidity-effect reanalysis. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolve derived the exact proximal identity Mtilde=SVT_lambda(P_Omega Y+P_missing Mtilde), the complete three-term local differential, and the rank-one projection quadratic map. For constant-factor MA(1) panels it derived a serial quadratic coefficient converging to -1/psi and an estimable Hessian--lag-covariance correction; a separate weak-signal block-mean case has exact remainder O_P(1/(n psi)) and oracle variance 36/n^2-64/n^3 versus iid 20/n^2. Hidden-block nonidentification, rank overprojection, window-growth boundaries, covariance degeneracy, residual contamination, and nearby literature were checked. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove uniform native-optimizer second-order transfer and plug-in stability, including centered quadratic aggregation and higher-order/regularization errors o(s), from primitive conditions. EARLY KILL TEST: At rank one with Gaussian MA(1), constant and positive alternating factors, H proportional to n, and psi=n^(4/5), reproduce the three-term derivative and exact quadratic coefficient, apply the fitted correction, and certify that n times the corrected native-optimizer remainder vanishes; a surviving interior term or strong-factor requirement forces pivot. seed_details.title: Native-optimizer curvature-corrected limit law for a growing-window causal contrast
seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, Section 3 and equation (3.1), Theorem 3.1, Proposition C.1 and its proof, and the Conclusion of arXiv:2308.02364 were read. The paper proves one-date subgroup inference for the rank-projected nuclear-norm estimator under independent errors; its proof exposes two leading score blocks and leaves serial dependence outside the theorem.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace the pointwise independent-noise decomposition after rank projection by a uniform second-order expansion of the masked singular-value-thresholding fixed point. The first derivative must retain donor-window, treated-pre, and donor-pre overlap scores, and the second derivative must be centered and corrected under finite-range serial covariance.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing deterministic block missingness, native nuclear-norm optimization, weak factors, serial dependence, growing post windows, and analytic curvature correction found no theorem with the full conjunction. Su, Wang, and Wang (2026) is the closest new collision, but its target is an interactive-effects regression coefficient and its final estimator is alternating maximization.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Choi and Yuan (2024) plus a finite-lag HAC because the target is only an average of their imputed cells.
seed_details.rebuttal: The published theorem is one-date and independent-noise; serial covariance creates a nonzero rank-projection quadratic drift, while growing aggregation promotes the omitted donor-pre differential and native-optimizer transfer error to the oracle standard-error scale.

seed_details.title: Sharp signal--cohort--window frontier for oracle-scale panel inference
seed_details.anchor_opened: The subgroup-size restrictions in Theorem 3.1, the weak-signal discussion in the Introduction, the decomposition in Proposition C.1, and the Conclusion of arXiv:2308.02364 were read. They establish an achievability region for small subgroups but do not characterize a three-way frontier for a growing consecutive window.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Track every inverse singular-value power and every cohort-window contraction in the native proximal expansion, then match the upper envelope with a relatively open rank-one Gaussian finite-range-dependent failure family.
seed_details.destination_search: Choi and Yuan (2025) index higher-order PCA remainders by signal strength; Armstrong, Weidner, and Zeleneev (2026) give weak-factor-uniform bias-aware regression inference; Xia and Yuan (2021) treat growing-support linear matrix forms under random sampling. None gives this native masked-optimizer three-way frontier.
seed_details.red_team: The frontier is merely the sufficient rate condition in Choi and Yuan rewritten with a window size.
seed_details.rebuttal: A sharp result requires both a native-optimizer upper theorem and a nondegenerate serial lower family locating the first uncorrectable term; neither direction is obtained by substituting a window size into the published pointwise condition.
seed_details.disposition: retained as the first-class open-ended question

seed_details.title: Influence-weighted residual finite-lag covariance and Hessian-drift estimation
seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, the loading-row central limit theorem, the two residual covariance constructions in Section 4, Theorem 4.3 and its proof discussion, and the terminal discussion of arXiv:2403.13153 were read. Its feasible HAC result concerns tensor loading scores and explicitly does not deliver common-component normality.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Decompose feasible-minus-oracle lag contractions into centered residual products, estimated influence weights, and native masked-optimizer contamination, then reuse the same lag estimates inside the second Fréchet-derivative drift.
seed_details.destination_search: Adjacent results by Xiong and Pelger (2023), Li, Shen, and Zhou (2024), and Su and Wang (2025) cover pointwise imputation, bootstrap intervals, or loading-row inference. None estimates both the aggregate score variance and a projection-Hessian drift for the Choi--Yuan estimator.
seed_details.red_team: Cen and Lam's residual HAC theorem applies after replacing their loading score by the ATT influence score.
seed_details.rebuttal: The ATT weights are estimated from overlapping masked optimizers and also enter a serial quadratic bias; the required feasible-oracle decomposition contains optimizer contamination and Hessian terms absent from their loading-row proof.

seed_details.title: Equivalence frontier between leave-neighbor auxiliary and native masked convex fits
seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, the auxiliary leave-one-out construction in Section 4, the feasible central limit theorem, the estimator-equivalence lemmas and their proofs, and the Conclusion of arXiv:2307.16370 were read. The auxiliary object is proof-only and is coupled to the implemented estimator under independent noise.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Differentiate the implicit masked proximal KKT map with respect to a whole serial neighborhood rather than delete one observation from a least-squares refit.
seed_details.destination_search: Choi and Yuan (2025) supplies neighborhood deletion for fully observed PCA, while Chen et al. (2020) supplies a convex-to-nonconvex bridge under random entry sampling. No exact observed-primitive divergence frontier for the causal block was found.
seed_details.red_team: This is the same leave-one-out equivalence lemma with a larger deleted set.
seed_details.rebuttal: Deleting a serial neighborhood perturbs the active singular spaces and the imputed part of the masked fixed point globally, so second-order aggregate equivalence is not implied by the pointwise lemma.
seed_details.disposition: dropped as a proof theorem rather than a stand-alone causal kernel

seed_details.title: Analytic-Wald versus block-bootstrap divergence for aggregated panel effects
seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, estimator construction, cellwise coverage theorem and proof, block wild bootstrap algorithm, and Conclusion of arXiv:2202.12078 were read. The proof lets the treated-cell shock dominate pointwise imputation error.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: For a growing window, replace the single treated shock by an influence-weighted serial sum and compare conditional bootstrap centering with the analytic projection-curvature correction.
seed_details.destination_search: No paper was found deriving an observed-primitive equivalence boundary between these two procedures for a weak-factor deterministic block. The available bootstrap target is nevertheless not the same structural cohort-window contrast.
seed_details.red_team: Standard block-bootstrap validity and Slutsky already imply equivalence with a consistent analytic variance estimator.
seed_details.rebuttal: That argument does not determine whether the bootstrap reproduces the estimator's serial quadratic centering, but the comparator's cellwise estimand makes the proposed frontier insufficiently clean.

seed_details.title: Growing-support linear-form inference under deterministic masking and serial noise
seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, double-debiasing construction, Theorem 4 and its alignment discussion, spectral-projector expansion in the proof, and terminal discussion of arXiv:1909.00116 were read. The theorem handles general linear forms under independent random entry sampling.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace random-sampling tangent isotropy by explicit donor and pre restricted Grams, then retain serial covariance contractions of the second spectral-projector derivative.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination pair of structured linear forms and deterministic causal masks is partially approached by Choi and Yuan (2024), but no general serial theorem was found.
seed_details.red_team: This is Xia and Yuan's linear-form theorem with deterministic weights.
seed_details.rebuttal: Deterministic block masking changes the inverse tangent operator and adds serial curvature, but the generic target sacrifices the concrete causal consumer available for the ATT kernel.
seed_details.disposition: dropped in favor of the concrete cohort-window target

seed_details.title: Weak-factor-uniform bias-aware inference for a common-start policy block
seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, nuclear-norm error theorem, minimax-linear construction, uniform confidence theorem and proof architecture, the common-start policy-indicator exclusion, and terminal discussion of arXiv:2210.06639 were read.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace regression residualization, which fails under low-rank collinearity of a common-start indicator, by counterfactual block completion with donor/pre restricted-Gram identification.
seed_details.destination_search: The search confirmed that the anchor deliberately excludes the relevant policy indicator. Choi and Yuan (2024) identifies the block through completion, but combining that identification with factor-uniform bias-aware inference would require a different full model.
seed_details.red_team: The anchor's exclusion is an identification failure, so changing the estimator cannot restore uniform inference without new information.
seed_details.rebuttal: Donor/pre span restrictions can supply that information, but doing so changes the published model enough that this is a separate, less feasible project.

seed_details.title: Serial growing-window inference for all-purpose missing-factor PCA
seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, adjusted-covariance estimator, pointwise common-component theorem, average-effect discussion, proof decomposition, and Conclusion of arXiv:1910.08273 were read. The estimator accommodates general missingness and dependence but uses a different PCA geometry.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Aggregate its pointwise loading and factor expansions over a consecutive causal window and retain cross-time score covariances at the aggregate scale.
seed_details.destination_search: Su and Wang (2025) advances general-missing factor inference, and Su, Wang, and Wang (2026) adds unbalanced-panel regression inference. Neither targets the Choi--Yuan weak-signal convex estimator.
seed_details.red_team: Weighted averages are already covered by summing the published pointwise influence functions.
seed_details.rebuttal: Uniform remainder and serial covariance control do not follow from pointwise expansions, but the estimator switch moves away from the topic's implemented procedure.
seed_details.disposition: dropped for consumer and estimator mismatch

seed_details.title: Leave-neighbor perturbation theory for an implicit masked proximal map
seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, leave-neighbor-out construction in the dependent-noise section, the weak-factor central limit theorem, recursive perturbation proof, and Conclusion of arXiv:2402.05789 were read. The method replaces a time neighborhood by signal in fully observed PCA.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Apply neighborhood replacement inside the imputed singular-value-thresholding fixed point and control changes of its KKT system and active singular subspaces.
seed_details.destination_search: Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2024) bridges an auxiliary object to a convex initializer, and Chen et al. (2020) controls an actual convex matrix-completion solution. Neither combines masked proximal sensitivity with serial neighborhood replacement.
seed_details.red_team: The implicit-function theorem for a spectrally separated proximal fixed point gives the result mechanically.
seed_details.rebuttal: The observation projector destroys global strong convexity and the growing signed aggregate requires uniform second-order, penalty, and active-space control beyond local differentiability.
